original_question: Do M-matrices satisfy Newton's inequalities c_j^2 >= c_{j-1} c_{j+1} for the normalized sums c_j of principal minors described in the paper's Newton-inequalities problem?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 5a, “Newton’s inequalities for M-matrices,” posed as a subproblem of Problem 5 on Newton’s inequalities for the normalized sums c_j of principal minors. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the M-matrix subproblem, the Newton inequality pattern c_j^2 ≥ c_{j-1}c_{j+1}, and the fact that the quantities c_j are the paper’s normalized sums of principal minors. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
missing_details: It should quantify explicitly over every matrix size n and every n×n matrix A in the class; Problem 5a is universal, not about a fixed matrix. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))

It should define c_j exactly as c_j := (1 / binom(n,j)) sum_{#α=j} A[α] for j=0,...,n, where A[α] denotes the principal minor det A(α,α). ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
To make c_0 precise, it should inherit the paper’s convention A[∅] := 1. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
It should state the full index range of the inequalities: j = 1,...,n−1. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))

A stand-alone version should not leave the term “M-matrix” completely implicit; the short note mentions M-matrices but does not define them there, so the standard matrix-theoretic meaning has to be supplied if full self-containment is desired. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))

It should avoid importing hypotheses not present in 5a itself, such as GKK, τ, stability, diagonalizability, or real-spectrum assumptions; those belong to surrounding discussion, not to the stated M-matrix subproblem. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))

There are no homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or “for all sufficiently large m” conditions in this problem; it is a finite-dimensional matrix question about principal minors. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
refined_question: For every n ≥ 1 and every n×n M-matrix A (in the standard matrix-theoretic sense), define c_j(A) := (1 / binom(n,j)) sum_{α⊆{1,...,n}, |α|=j} det A(α,α) for j=0,...,n, with c_0(A)=1 via A[∅]:=1. Must A satisfy the Newton inequalities c_j(A)^2 ≥ c_{j-1}(A)c_{j+1}(A) for every j=1,...,n−1? ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
justification: The closest official target is the paper’s subproblem 5a, not the broader Problem 5 about GKK τ-matrices. Section 3 supplies the exact c_j notation and the inequality template, and Section 2 supplies the principal-minor notation A[α] together with A[∅]:=1. The note does not state an explicit equivalent reformulation of 5a, so none should be added. Your draft is already close to the paper’s intent, but it leaves the quantifiers, normalization, j-range, and the external standard meaning of “M-matrix” implicit. ([people.math.wisc.edu](https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/paper_archive/other_papers/hs144.pdf))
